item.title: Trump Tells European Leaders That Putin Wants Peace
item.description: US President Donald Trump offered a triumphant assessment of his conversation with Vladimir Putin in a surprise phone call to European leaders gathered in Berlin, arguing the Russian leader wants to end the war. Bloomberg's Greg Sullivan has more. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Three Kyiv Bridges Hit by Russia after Putin Vowed Revenge for Crimean Bridge
item.description: Russian ballistic missiles damaged three bridges across the Dnipro River in Kyiv overnight, hours after President Vladimir Putin vowed revenge for the destruction of a crossing that links Russia to Crimea.
item.dc:creator: Yurii Stasiuk

item.title: UK Won't Simply Follow EU on China Tariffs, Reynolds Says
item.description: UK Trade Secretary Jonathan Reynolds said Britain is interested in having a dialogue with the European Union on how to tackle common problems like overcapacity and unfair trade practices, but wouldn't simply follow the EU's tariff approach on countries like China. Speaking to Bloomberg ahead of Andy Burnham's meeting with EU leaders in Brussels, Reynolds also defended the prime minister's approach of raising the prospect of rejoining the bloc. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Xi’s Playlist for World Leaders Dissected for Goodwill, Insults
item.description: In imperial China, emperors retained a “Minister of Rites” to ensure every detail of royal ceremony was just so. The office is long gone, but its spirit seemed alive at this week’s gathering of world leaders in Shenzhen — right down to the music.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: Parag Khanna: Globalization Isn’t Dead
item.description: Global trade wars and immigration backlash have fueled predictions of globalization’s demise. Geostrategist Parag Khanna tells Mishal Husain why he thinks it will still prevail. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: White House Dismisses Trump’s Cyber Security Chief Cairncross
item.description: President Donald Trump’s national cyber director has departed his role, a major shakeup as the administration downplays a series of technical failures across the country.
item.dc:creator: Josh Wingrove and John Harney

item.title: Senate Passes Landmark Bill to Overhaul US Energy Permitting
item.description: The US Senate passed a landmark bill to make it easier to build pipelines, power lines and other major energy infrastructure, sending the measure to the House, where its future remains uncertain.
item.dc:creator: Ari Natter

item.title: Thune Sees Debt Limit Hike as Next Year’s Fight, Semafor Reports
item.description: Senate Majority Leader John Thune says it’s unlikely that Republican lawmakers will seek to raise the debt limit while they still have the majority for the rest of this year, adding in an interview with Semafor that the issue “probably ends up getting punted” into 2027.
item.dc:creator: Derek Wallbank

item.title: Documents Released by House Panel Show AI Chip Approvals
item.description: "Balance of Power" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, EqualAI President Miriam Vogel says Anthropic’s IPO puts frontier AI labs under greater scrutiny from investors and regulators, as pressure builds in Washington for clearer guardrails around the technology. Nicholas Burns, who served as US Ambassador to China under President Biden and previously as US Ambassador to NATO, says President Trump’s trilateral meeting with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin sent the wrong message to US allies, while warning that tensions over Nvidia and chip exports could further strain relations with Beijing. Republican Representative Marlin Stutzman of Indiana criticized GOP lawmakers for missing votes as the party races to finish its agenda before losing the House majority, telling absent colleagues to “get back to work.” (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Spain’s Sánchez Struggles in Debate Against Main Rival Feijóo
item.description: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez sought to brush off attacks from opposition leader Alberto Núñez Feijóo in an electoral debate Thursday by apologising for corruption in his government and for two large train accidents.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Basteiro

item.title: Burnham Heads to Brussels: What to Expect From UK-EU Summit
item.description: Andy Burnham will meet with European Union leaders on Friday to seal a deal for closer ties as part of a post-Brexit reset that the UK Prime Minister has said he wants to go even further.
item.dc:creator: Chloe Chaplain, Jorge Valero and Lucy White

item.title: Rep. Stutzman: GOP Must Finish Strong in Lame Duck
item.description: Republican Representative Marlin Stutzman of Indiana criticized GOP lawmakers for missing votes as the party races to finish its agenda before losing the House majority, telling absent colleagues to “get back to work.” He also pointed to unfinished business on spending, defense, permitting and the debt ceiling. He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Fmr. Amb. Criticizes Trump-Xi-Putin Summit Optics
item.description: Nicholas Burns, who served as US Ambassador to China under President Biden and previously as US Ambassador to NATO, says President Trump’s trilateral meeting with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin sent the wrong message to US allies, while warning that tensions over Nvidia and chip exports could further strain relations with Beijing. He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Bloomberg Businessweek Daily Podcast: Anthropic IPO
item.description:
The people, companies and trends shaping the global economy. Watch Carol and Tim LIVE every day on YouTube: http://bit.ly/3vTiACF
Anthropic shares pared earlier gains to trade 17% above their IPO price after the artificial intelligence lab’s blockbuster $107.3 billion debut broke SpaceX’s record for the biggest-ever offering. The shares were changing hands at $96.75 each at 1:29 p.m. on Thursday in New York, after an opening surge that took it far above the IPO price of $83. The current price gives Anthropic a fully diluted market value of about $1.8 trillion, making it one of the 10 biggest public companies in the world by market cap, rivaling SpaceX and briefly challenging Amazon.com Inc. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Australian Leader to Navigate Trade, Security in China Talks
item.description: Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese will aim to navigate delicate security and trade issues when he meets with China’s top leadership on Friday, seeking to ease access for commodities to its biggest export partner.
item.dc:creator: James Mayger

item.title: Trump Calls Skeptical Allies to Sell View Putin Wants Peace
item.description: US President Donald Trump offered a triumphant assessment of his conversation with Vladimir Putin in a surprise phone call to European leaders gathered in Berlin, arguing the Russian leader wants to end the war.
item.dc:creator: Andra Timu, Alberto Nardelli, Ott Tammik and Arne Delfs

item.title: White House Took Reporters’ Phones as Trump Departed China
item.description: The White House took phones away from reporters traveling with President Donald Trump upon his departure from China, an unusual move.
item.dc:creator: Jeff Mason and Courtney Subramanian

item.title: India, Japan Deepen Defense Ties Amid China, US Uncertainty
item.description: Japan and India are deepening cooperation in underwater and missile technologies as China expands its military presence across the region and concerns over the durability of US commitments in the Indo-Pacific.
item.dc:creator: Sudhi Ranjan Sen

item.title: Takaichi Walks Tightrope With Russia, China on Asia Trip
item.description: Sanae Takaichi’s trip to China for an international summit alongside rivals Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin went better than expected. Now, the question is whether she can break the diplomatic deadlock with them.
item.dc:creator: Alastair Gale and Sakura Murakami

item.title: Xi Embraces Trump as China’s Best Option to Contain Chip Row
item.description: Xi Jinping showed Donald Trump extraordinary hospitality during their third summit of the year. For Beijing, that bonhomie might be its best strategy for stopping a spiraling chip battle with its main rival.
item.dc:creator: Nectar Gan and Annmarie Hordern
